The FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop just before 4 p.m. ET Friday, halting departures at every U.S. airport "due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety." Planes already in the air were allowed to land. Flightradar24 data mapped by meteorologist Ryan Hall shows about 2,160 passenger planes over the U.S. at 3:53 p.m. By 5:08 p.m., 778 were left. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called it a telecommunications outage and said there is no indication it was a threat to the United States. The FBI is looking at whether a software update caused it and doesn't believe it was a cyberattack, Bloomberg reported. #fyp #americanstriker #trending #faa #flights
